audit_findings.title: Finance-lease assets may bypass the reinvestment deduction
audit_findings.magnitude: $201 million of 2025 finance-lease additions and $95 million of 2025 leased-asset amortization; exact maintenance portion unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: OE adds back depreciation and amortization while the reinvestment deduction appears limited to cash capital expenditures, allowing lease-financed replacement assets to avoid an offsetting charge.
audit_findings.evidence: Transportation equipment included $ 717 million and $ 641 million of financing lease assets as of December 27, 2025 and December 28, 2024, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: The accounting mismatch is demonstrated: filed D&A includes finance-lease amortization, while $201 million of leased assets were acquired without entering cash capital expenditures. The record does not establish how much was maintenance rather than growth investment, but even the $95 million amortization component equals 12.9% of the $734.1 million anchor and is reasonably capable of materially reducing every scenario.
audit_findings.action: Reconstruct 2025 maintenance investment including noncash finance-lease additions by asset class, or remove finance-lease amortization from the D&A add-back, and rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: Future interest cost is embedded but apparently not modeled
audit_findings.magnitude: $19 million per year for each 1 percentage-point rate change, equal to 2.6% of anchor OE before any tax effect
audit_findings.mechanism: Interest expense is retained in equity-level OE, so floating rates, refinancing rates, and changes in borrowings alter forecast OE directly.
audit_findings.evidence: A hypothetical 1% change in the applicable rate would cause the interest expense on our floating rate debt to change by approximately $19 million per year (see Note 9, Debt, in our consolidated financial statements).
audit_findings.explanation: FY2025 OE already contains $305 million of net interest expense, and first-half 2026 interest was $152 million versus $151 million in the comparable period. No present omission is demonstrated, but applying a single growth rate to total OE does not separately model future financing costs. Rates could raise or lower value, and refinancing effects beyond the filed sensitivity are unquantified.
audit_findings.action: Build an after-tax interest schedule using the June 2026 debt balances, contractual maturities, rate caps through April 2027, scenario refinancing rates, and any assumed borrowing changes; then rerun OE forecasts.

audit_findings.title: The share denominator postdates the earnings numerator
audit_findings.magnitude: 4.329643 million-share difference between the 220.660366 million fully diluted denominator and the 216.330723 million July cover count, or 2.0%; denominator-only base value would be about $47.93 rather than $47.00
audit_findings.mechanism: The denominator determines value per share, while repurchase funding can also affect bridge cash, debt, and future interest expense.
audit_findings.evidence: 220,541,957 shares of the registrant’s common stock were outstanding as of February 6, 2026.
audit_findings.explanation: The dates are mismatched, but the valuation uses the June 2026 cash and debt balances that already reflect $445 million of first-half repurchases, substantially addressing the associated funding side. The fully diluted denominator is only 0.118409 million above the 220.541957 million fiscal-year-end cover count. Even substituting the lower July cover count without dilution raises base value by only about $0.93 per share and cannot bridge the $48.64 gap between the $104.04 market price and the $55.40 bull value. Any July funding mismatch remains unquantified.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the 216.330723 million July cover count to the 220.660366 million fully diluted count and confirm July repurchases, award dilution, cash, debt, and interest; rerun only if the reconciliation identifies an omitted capital transaction.

audit_findings.title: Gross cash may be offset by an omitted cash-overdraft claim
audit_findings.magnitude: $168 million latest cash-overdraft liability, equivalent to $0.76 per diluted share and 1.6% of base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: If the overdraft is financing or a claim against bridge cash, gross cash should be reduced by the overdraft in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: The carrying value of cash, accounts receivable, vendor receivables, cash overdraft liability and accounts payable approximate their fair values due to their short-term maturities.
audit_findings.explanation: The latest 10-Q demonstrates that the $168 million overdraft remained outstanding while the bridge adds $56 million of gross cash and does not list the overdraft. Its economic classification is unresolved. Even treating the entire overdraft as an omitted equity claim would reduce each scenario by only about $0.76 per share and would not change the valuation conclusion relative to the $104.04 market price.
audit_findings.action: Confirm whether the overdraft represents outstanding checks and operating float or interest-bearing financing and whether it is contractually nettable against cash; if not operating float, deduct $168 million in a bridge rerun.

audit_findings.title: Projected growth may require acquisition spending excluded from OE
audit_findings.magnitude: $541 million of acquisition cash spending in 2023-2025, averaging $180.3 million annually or 24.6% of anchor OE
audit_findings.mechanism: Acquired earnings enter consolidated OE and its historical growth, but acquisition purchase payments are excluded from the capital-expenditure deduction; forecast growth can therefore be credited without its required acquisition investment.
audit_findings.evidence: Historically, a portion of our growth has come through acquisitions.
audit_findings.explanation: Acquisition spending and its exclusion from cash capital expenditures are demonstrated, including $131 million in 2025, $214 million in 2024, and $196 million in 2023. It remains unresolved whether the 3% and 6% forecasts assume acquisition-assisted growth. The historical spending scale is large relative to the $734.1 million anchor, so an acquisition requirement could materially reduce the growth-case values.
audit_findings.action: Decompose historical OE growth into organic, acquired, and synergy components; either support forecast growth entirely from organic operations and deducted reinvestment or include a normalized acquisition-spending charge and rerun the base and bull cases.

audit_findings.title: Residual-value guarantees could create an unrecorded lease claim
audit_findings.magnitude: up to $265 million of filed residual-value guarantees; unrecorded and expected-loss portions unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Payments not already included in lease liabilities would reduce future OE or require an additional equity-bridge claim if residual values fall short.
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 27, 2025, lease agreements included residual value guarantees of up to $ 265 million that could potentially come due in future periods.
audit_findings.explanation: The guarantees are contingent and only probable amounts are included in recorded lease measurements, so no present valuation error or expected loss is demonstrated. The filed maximum exposure equals about $1.20 per diluted share if incurred in full, but the probability, timing, collateral coverage, and unrecorded portion are unavailable.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the guarantee schedule by asset, expiration date, contractual floor, current market residual value, and amount already included in lease liabilities; recognize a normalized OE charge or bridge liability if a probable recurring shortfall emerges.
